drops.reason: CVSS 10.0 pre-auth prefix-rewrite bypass but no exploitation, no public PoC, no scanning; library-level fix (upgrade 11.6.0) is a routine dependency bump — fails the strict vulnerability gate (action beyond regular patch cycle); high CVSS alone insufficient.

Only new element is a single-source unconfirmed watchTowr-CEO 'first indications of ITW' claim (no KEV, no named victim, no telemetry); prior 07-18 entry already carries the dual-route WAF mitigation and correctly declines to claim ITW. Fails two-source/fake-news bar; no material new development.

Prior 07-17 entry already carries CISA's AMSI/MDAV signatures, machineKey-theft framing, and hunt-before-rotate guidance. Only incremental content is Resecurity's (C-tier, explicitly-fictional 'Operation FarmKey') farm-account SQL-role pivot — deeper analysis of already-covered exploitation, not a material new development; no new CVE/victim/exploitation-status change.

The ShadowByt3$/LabCentral second incident is already covered in the 07-18 Abbott entry from the same BleepingComputer source; the API-exfil detail is same-source backfill, not a new development. Duplicate.

Unconfirmed criminal/leak claim, no SFR confirmation, no independent A/B verification; a circulated 'SFR confirmed' quote traces to a recycled Dec-2025 SFR breach (conflation trap). Fails two-source/fake-news bar for leak-site claims.

drops.item: German cluster: Wiesbaden DDoS + Netze BW/Stuttgart Netze meter-contractor breach (S2)
drops.reason: DDoS part low-value (municipal availability, restored; Mainz was a DNS fault not an attack). Meter-contractor breach is 2.5-3 days old and its transferable third-party-meter-supplier lesson duplicates the already-covered IWB Basel entry; the recurring-German-pattern framing is strategic/weekly material, not operational. A CH energy-CI defender would not act differently in 7 days.
